title: Reaching the Bus Stop
transcript:
The poster is easy to follow, but what does the shaded area around each bus stop actually represent?
It shows the streets we could reach within five minutes on foot. We timed the routes ourselves last Thursday.
That explains the boundary. What feature did you look for where people had to cross the road?
We checked for dropped kerbs on both sides. A crossing was marked as accessible only if both sides had them.
Could you make the stop symbols easier to recognise? They look quite similar at this size.
I'll put a legend beneath the map. There's space where I originally planned to put the route timetable.
What surprised you most when you compared the stops themselves?
The busiest stop had nowhere to sit, although two quieter ones had benches.
Put that observation beside the map. It gives readers a concrete reason to look beyond how close the stops are.

questions.prompt: The shaded area represents the streets within a walk of ____ from each stop.
questions.explanation: 学生说阴影标出了从每个站点步行五分钟内可达的街道。

questions.prompt: A crossing was marked as accessible if it had ____ on both sides.
questions.explanation: 学生说只有道路两侧都有下沉式路缘的过街点才被标为无障碍。

questions.prompt: The student will add a ____ beneath the map to explain its symbols.
questions.explanation: 学生计划在地图下方添加图例，帮助读者辨认符号。

questions.prompt: What surprised the student about the busiest stop?
options: It had an unusually long waiting area.
It was served by fewer routes than expected.
questions.explanation: 学生发现最繁忙的车站没有座位，而两个较冷清的车站设有长椅。

questions.prompt: Where does the tutor suggest displaying the surprising observation?
questions.explanation: 导师建议把这条发现放在地图旁边。
